title: edge-fix transform rule
description: One executable graph rewrite. The agent builds the engine; the owner authors the rules — the engine never invents transforms beyond clearly-marked example-provenance rules exercised only on synthetic fixtures. `action` is a CLOSED vocabulary (v1: replace_op, decompose, insert_cast, io_cast); anything not expressible in it is not a rule — the vocabulary is extended by spec amendment, not by freeform actions. A matrix rewrite_hints entry links to a rule via its `transform_id` (matrix schema 1.2). Rule files are named `<id>.json`. Schema 1.1 (Phase 11, additive): optional `stale` block, written by `edge-fix rules reverify` when the rule's declared fixture stops passing against a new runtime version — stale rules are flagged in place and listed in DELTA_LOG.md, never auto-deleted; a later passing reverify removes the block.

schema_version.description: 1.1 (Phase 11, additive): optional `stale` re-verification flag. A rule carrying `stale` must declare 1.1; 1.0 documents without it remain valid.

id.description: Rule identity: referenced by fix reports and by matrix rewrite_hints[].transform_id. The rule file must be named <id>.json.

params.description: Action-specific parameters; shape constrained per action by the allOf clauses below.

expected_effect.description: What the fix should achieve, verified by the re-lint improvement gate (e.g. 'op delegates; single contiguous partition').

notes.description: Validity caveats: the conditions under which the rewrite preserves semantics (e.g. 'exact only for non-negative operands'). Surfaced verbatim in fix reports.

evidence.description: Where this rewrite was observed to work. Required fields for measured rules are enforced by semantic lint in `edge-fix rules validate`.

fixture.description: The rule's own demonstration fixture, paths relative to the rule file. `edge-fix rules validate` dry-runs the rule against it and requires the fix to succeed end-to-end.

stale.description: Written by `edge-fix rules reverify` (schema 1.1) when the declared fixture stops passing against `runtime` at `runtime_version` — a measured re-verification failure, never a guess. The rule stays in place (never auto-deleted); a passing reverify removes this block. Listed in the DELTA_LOG.md entry (spec 11.4).

params.description: Swap the matched node's operator in place; inputs and outputs are kept verbatim. The engine attaches the registered default builtin options for new_op and refuses ops outside its options registry.

nodes.description: Fixed recipe of replacement nodes, in execution order. Tensor refs: in:K / out:K are the matched node's K-th input/output tensor; tmp:NAME is a declared intermediate. A RESHAPE node names exactly one (data) input — the engine synthesizes its constant int32 shape input from the node's declared output tensor, whose shape must be static.

intermediates.description: New intermediate tensors. Shapes are always derived from a matched tensor — like:in:K / like:out:K borrow it as-is, unsqueeze0:in:K / unsqueeze0:out:K borrow it with a leading unit axis prepended (rank+1; the source shape must be static). No freeform shapes, so recipes stay statically checkable.

params.description: Compute the matched node in dtype `to`: CAST is inserted on every input edge whose dtype differs, the node's own tensors move to `to`, and outputs are CAST back to their original dtypes.

match.description: io_cast matches graph I/O tensors by dtype, not nodes: match.dtypes lists the offending interface dtypes; op / op_sequence are not allowed.

params.description: Wrap graph I/O to satisfy interface constraints (e.g. LiteRT.js float32/int32 tensor I/O): matched graph inputs/outputs are re-exposed in dtype `to` with a CAST at the boundary; the interior graph is unchanged.

match.description: Base match shape; each action's allOf clause tightens it (node actions require exactly one of op/op_sequence, io_cast requires dtypes and forbids op).

op_name.description: Exact TFLite builtin operator name. No aliases, no prettified names.

constraints.description: Same semantics as matrix entry constraints: matched against the node's shape_meta (max_rank/min_rank compare numerically, other keys by equality).

op_sequence.description: A chain of consecutive ops in execution order. Accepted by the schema as part of the public rule API; the v1 engine does not execute op_sequence rules and reports them as refused (Deferred).

node_match.description: Which lint findings this rule addresses: nodes with this op (or op chain) whose verdict is not `delegated`, narrowed by dtypes (node signature dtypes must be a subset) and constraints (matched against shape_meta).
